chunks: Abu Basir narrated from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:

Indeed, the believing servant asks Allah, majestic is His glory, for a need, and Allah, mighty and majestic, delays the fulfillment of his need which he asked for until the Day of Jumu'ah, so that He may single him out with the merit of the Day of Jumu'ah.

key_terms.اللَّهَ: Allah, the One asked and the One who fulfills needs
key_terms.الْحَاجَةَ: a need or request sought from Allah
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ الْمُؤْمِنَ: the believing servant who turns to Allah in faith
key_terms.بِفَضْلِ: with the special virtue, bounty, or merit
key_terms.قَضَاءَ حَاجَتِهِ: the fulfillment or completion of his need
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ: the Day of Jumu'ah, a day of special merit and blessing

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah sometimes delay answering a believer’s du'a until Friday?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that a believer’s du'a may be delayed not as a denial, but as a form of divine favor. Allah may postpone fulfilling a need until Friday so that the servant receives the added blessing and merit associated with that day.
